abstract_sentences.text: Neural networks (NNs) often have critical behavioural trade-offs that are set at design time with hyperparameters—such as reward weights in reinforcement learning or quantile targets in regression.
abstract_sentences.handoff: design-time trade-offs lead to post-deployment mismatch

abstract_sentences.text: Post-deployment, however, user preferences can evolve, making initial settings undesirable, necessitating potentially expensive retraining.

To circumvent this, we introduce the task of Hyperparameter Trajectory Inference (HTI): to learn, from observed data, how a NN’s conditional output distribution changes with its hyperparameters, and construct a surrogate model that approximates the NN at unobserved hyperparameter settings.

evidence.anchor: introduce the task of Hyperparameter Trajectory Inference

abstract_sentences.text: HTI requires extending existing trajectory inference approaches to incorporate conditions, exacerbating the challenge of ensuring inferred paths are feasible.

We propose an approach based on conditional Lagrangian optimal transport, jointly learning the Lagrangian function governing hyperparameter-induced dynamics along with the associated optimal transport maps and geodesics between observed marginals, which form the surrogate model.
We incorporate inductive biases based on the manifold hypothesis and least-action principles into the learned Lagrangian, improving surrogate model feasibility.
We empirically demonstrate that our approach reconstructs NN outputs across various hyperparameter spectra better than other alternatives.

experimental_design.name: common_reporting
experimental_design.description: All results are averaged over 20 runs and reported with standard errors; detailed settings move to Appendix C.

experimental_design.name: synthetic_semicircles
experimental_design.description: Four conditional noised semicircles train at t={0,0.5,1}; 100 samples per condition/time; held-out t={0.25,0.75}; NLL and circle distance evaluate variants.

experimental_design.name: cancer_reward_weighting
experimental_design.description: DTR-Bench Cancer PPO policies at lambda_NK={0,5,10} provide anchors; eight intermediate lambda_NK settings are held out; Direct, CFM, MFM, NLOT, and component variants are compared.

experimental_design.name: reacher_reward_weighting
experimental_design.description: OpenAI Gym Reacher PPO uses lambda_c={1,5} anchors and {2,3,4} held-out settings; ground-truth policies train for 1,000,000 timesteps.

experimental_design.name: nonlinear_cancer
experimental_design.description: Cancer_nonlin uses the Cancer protocol with a hinge NK penalty active above relative deviation 0.01.

experimental_design.name: ettm2_quantile_regression
experimental_design.description: Endpoint tau=.01/.99 forecasters form HTI anchors; five intermediate quantiles on 180 later chronological test inputs are compared with true-NN outputs using MSE.

experimental_design.name: dropout_diffusion
experimental_design.description: Two-moons DDPMs at p={0,.5,.99} supply 1,000 samples per anchor; eight intermediate dropout levels use Wasserstein distance to target diffusion samples.

experimental_design.name: reproducibility_assets
experimental_design.description: Appendix C reports Azure A100, approximately 120 final GPU hours, hyperparameters, implementation sources, and task-specific times; the paper links released code.

final_judgment.single_storyline: HTI treats hyperparameter-induced conditional output paths as conditional trajectory inference, learns a Lagrangian cost with dense-traversal and least-action biases, and samples a surrogate at unseen continuous lambda.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Task definition, COT/CLOT derivation, U-hat/GthetaG/maps/spline training and sampling, main comparisons, and the one-continuous-hyperparameter boundary remain in the main body.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix C holds exact generators, reward definitions, splits, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, and baseline implementations; Appendix E holds anchor-sparsity evidence; Appendix D expands the multiple-hyperparameter boundary.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A controlled geometric mechanism ablation in Figure 1/Table 1 precedes application tables and reuses the same variant vocabulary across domains.
final_judgment.largest_gap: No theorem/guarantee is supplied; main rankings use 20-run means and standard errors without seed identities or pairwise tests; two figures have undefined shaded bands; the dropout reversal requires cross-table synthesis.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claimed inductive bias, first give a controlled experiment in which its geometric or mechanistic consequence is separable, then extend with application comparisons using the same component labels.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: A controlled geometry supports only its stated path and sparsity regime; multi-hyperparameter, chaotic, deployment, and cost claims need their own direct evidence.
final_judgment.body_self_sufficiency: Main text supports the decision-level method/result narrative; exact reproducibility and the sparsity robustness conclusion require Appendix C/E.
final_judgment.theory_role: Core causal construction and explanation, not a formal performance guarantee.
